findings.title: WHITEARMOR SHAKES DOWN SHIPPING GIANT FOR $5M
findings.comment: A crew that admits its encryptor "ain't quite ready yet" still wants five million in doubloons for a legacy system nobody remembered existed either, matey.

findings.title: SOUTHWIRE CONFIRMS HEALTH DATA WALKED OUT THE DOOR
findings.comment: Files sailed off between November and January and nobody noticed til late January - that's not a breach, that's a squatter's rights claim.

findings.title: GOODBODY PORTAL DARK FOR THIRD STRAIGHT DAY
findings.comment: "No impact to client funds" is the thing every stockbroker says right up until the forensics report arrives with bad news, savvy.

findings.title: QILIN BOARDS UT ARLINGTON, LEAKS LIBRARY LOOT
findings.comment: Qilin claims the library server, which tracks roughly with its usual taste for targets that can't afford a ransom but also can't afford the lawsuits after.

findings.title: INCRANSOM CLAIMS COEUR MINING, THREATENS DATA DUMP
findings.comment: Incransom wants ransom for a mining company's data, proving once again that extortion crews will dig for treasure anywhere, including silver mines.

findings.title: N0N CREW LISTS DANISH PHARMA GIANT LEO PHARMA
findings.comment: A fresh-faced extortion outfit nobody's heard of posts a pharma titan on its wall of shame - instant credibility by proxy, ye scurvy marketing trick.

findings.title: VEXY RANSOMWARE CLAIMS BRAZILIAN FIRM UPPER WEB
findings.comment: Another day, another freshly christened crew flying a new flag over someone else's stolen cargo - the RaaS factory never sleeps, arrr.

findings.title: OPERATION TORNADO NABS 354 DARK-WEB VENDORS
findings.comment: Fourteen kingdoms swing the cutlass at 354 peddlers of poison from Archetyp, Bohemia, Tor2Door and mates — $234M hauled off, though these bazaars always sprout new sails.

findings.title: OPERATION ENDGAME SEIZES 6.4M STOLEN RECORDS
findings.comment: Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC galleons boarded across nine seas; 6.4 million purloined ledgers fished from the hold before the credential brokers could fence 'em.

findings.title: REMUS STEALER SELLS 'PERSISTENT' GMAIL ACCESS
findings.comment: A stealer hawkers Gmail doors that "survive password changes" at a grand a month for the fancy tier — though Hudson Rock squints hard and finds no map marks that treasure.

findings.title: DEAD 2013 CRIME FORUM BREACH LANDS ON HIBP
findings.comment: A dozen years down the brine, YouHack's 7.2 million drowned emails wash ashore on HIBP — unsalted MD5, the laziest lock ever fitted to a ship.

findings.title: eBPF ROOTKIT RECIPES TRADED UNDERGROUND
findings.comment: The Duty Free bazaar now hands out rootkit scrolls that hide from the very crew inspecting the hold — free recipes, bring yer own C2.

findings.title: BARRACUDA ROOT-RCE CHAIN ON CISA KEV, 3-DAY DEADLINE
findings.comment: CISA dropped six exploited flaws in the KEV, an' the Barracuda email-gateway chain (auth bypass plus root command injection) got a federal deadline of TODAY, Nov 13. Three days to patch or yer gateway walks the plank.

findings.title: CHROME EMERGENCY PATCH FOR EIGHTH ZERO-DAY OF 2026
findings.comment: CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free in Chrome's XML guts, exploited in the wild an' fixed in 157.0.8103.50. Eighth zero-day this year, so relaunch the browser, ye deck-swabbers, auto-update dawdles like a drunk first mate.

findings.title: PATCH TUESDAY: 1,093 CVES WITH EXPLOITED OUTLOOK ZERO-DAY
findings.comment: A record 1,093 CVEs, but the one already bein' plundered is CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook spoof that swipes NTLMv2 hashes with no warning prompt. Credited to a researcher wieldin' an LLM, no less. The robots fight both sides now.

findings.title: SIGNDROP: UNPATCHED WINDOWS CLFS LPE POC GOES PUBLIC
findings.comment: MSNightmare turned Microsoft's own CLFS authentication shield into a SYSTEM shell an' posted the PoC, with no patch or CVE in sight. Hunt fer stray .cnpf files spawned by Defender an' ERROR_LOG_METADATA_CORRUPT errors.

findings.title: SCREENCONNECT PROBE: 400 MSP PARTNERS ORDERED TO RESET
findings.comment: ConnectWise flagged a rogue RMM+ extension in some 400 partner fleets, an' its remedy list reads like a keelhaul: clients to 26.6.5, credentials revoked, MFA on, EDR sweeps out-of-band. Third-party plugins be the barnacles on every hull.

findings.title: FIREFOX 160 SHIPS 99 FIXES INCLUDING SANDBOX ESCAPES
findings.comment: Ninety-nine holes, 57 rated high, multiple sandbox escapes. A fat cluster carries the credit o' OpenAI's Codex Security agent, so the machines be auditin' the machines. Update browser an' ESR fleets alike.

findings.title: IVANTI NOVEMBER UPDATE SPANS FIVE PRODUCTS, SIX CVES
findings.comment: Six CVEs across UWM, Sentry, EPMM, CSA an' EPM, none exploited yet. Ivanti admits LLM-assisted testin' found bugs the classical scanners missed, so expect the disclosure tide to keep risin'. Patch now, whine later.

findings.title: FACESTEALER INFRASTRUCTURE SEIZED
findings.comment: Feds swiped 900 secret webcam videos from BlueNoroff's cloud locker, sinking a $400M deepfake call scam — arrr, that be a mighty fine trophy wall.

findings.title: WHITEARMOR DEMANDS $5M
findings.comment: The gang claims 100GB and 30,000 driver records from a dusty legacy logistics platform; Maersk calls it a scratch on the hull. We shall see.

findings.title: SIX US LENDERS CLAIMED
findings.comment: Storm claims five banks and a credit union, two confess; a managed-IT provider looks like the rowboat that carried the boarding party aboard.

findings.title: "NON" CLAIMS AWS MEGA-BREACH
findings.comment: A lone handle "non" claims the Wiz-Mandiant cloud pillage of Qubole customers, then vanishes into the fog like a proper ghost ship — no proof, all swagger.

findings.title: FAKE COURT NOTICES SPREAD RAT
findings.comment: APT-C-36 fires 3,300 phishing broadsides dressed as Colombian court summons, smuggling an AsyncRAT stowaway past email cannons. Gavel, meet keyboard.

findings.title: FRANCE ACCUSES OVER FRIDGE MASSACRE
findings.comment: CISA and four agencies warn food retailers after spoiled-stock attacks; Paris openly blames the IRGC for cooking French supermarkets' produce.

findings.title: BYOD GANG CLAIMS 1M SSNs
findings.comment: Fresh-faced BYOD crew, afloat since September, claims a full domain-controller plunder of Vanderbilt including a million SSNs; the university confirms the storm but not the loot.

findings.title: OUTLOOK ZERO-DAY STEALS NTLM HASHES
findings.comment: Open one crafted message file and Outlook sails authentication data to an attacker share—moderate score, high exploitation, classic spreadsheet arithmetic.

findings.title: CHROME ZERO-DAY EXPLOITED IN THE WILD
findings.comment: Chrome’s XML use-after-free reached live attacks before disclosure; update to 157.0.8103.50 or .51, lest freed memory become someone else’s treasure chest.

findings.title: ANONYMOUS RCE CHAIN FULLY DISCLOSED
findings.comment: Several sandbox and permission failures chain into anonymous server code execution back to Plone 4.3; one tiny portal_modifier clue reportedly yielded an exploit path in minutes.

findings.title: BARRACUDA ESG CHAIN REACHES ROOT
findings.comment: Attackers chained authorization bypass with CVE-2026-111560 command injection for root on exposed admin interfaces—an email gateway welcoming boarders personally.
